headline: Why can't I stop thinking about him?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every ban in this note still stands.

Face-down only (return-mhf). 🔴 NO DIRECTIVE — 'let him go', 'time to move on', 'try to forget him' are what she has been told by everyone already, and they are not a reading. 🔴 No promise about him and 🔴 no pathologising: obsessed, unhealthy, 'you are stuck' are all banned. 🔴 No timeframe.

Finding, kept distinct from its two siblings: the word 'stop'. She has framed her own mind as a machine she is failing to switch off, and has been trying to win by force. Minds do not take orders — and the trying is costing more than the thinking.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — both his hands are busy and neither is resting.
You asked why you can't stop thinking about him. Your hand went to the man who can't put it down.
So you've been trying to stop by force, dear. That's the tiring bit.
And his hands are busy, dear, with no off switch anywhere on him.
But a mind doesn't take orders like that, dear. Not one.
That's why the trying costs you more than the thinking does, dear.
Let me look closer at what has kept you fighting your own head…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — he's quite still and nothing about him is resolved.
You asked why you can't stop thinking about him. Your hand went to the card that stays open.
So this is still open, dear. That's the whole of it.
And nothing is closed off on his card, dear. Nothing put away.
But open things keep asking to be closed, dear.
That's why he turns up at two in the morning, dear. Nobody asked him.
Let me look closer at what has held this open…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — the road under him runs right up to the edge.
You asked why you can't stop thinking about him. Your hand went to the one who walks with it.
So he walks and thinks at once, dear. He stops for neither.
And he's moving, dear, with the whole load still on his back.
But you were told to stop before you could carry on, dear.
That's why stopping felt like the only way out, dear. It never was.
Let me look closer at what made stopping the only option…
